It is done, and submitted. You can play “Survival of the Flats” online or offline, which is fun for those of you who don’t have a 3D printer. The game has a lot of mechanics in it, including three base game scenarios, two player scenarios, and online scenarios, so play around with how you want to play.

The most important thing to remember is the game is about a new ecosystem coming together with its own rules. These “rules”, as they were first described, are the Survival of the Flats collaboration rules. By the time you read this, the full article has already been published (or will be published). With the article, the idea and mission have changed. The article discusses our plans for the game, but lets not remind myself of any future, or even yesterday’s, dates.

There were two reasons for my decision to change the collaborative guidelines. The first reason was to be a bit more forgiving in the collaborative rules, and the second was to allow space for everyone to play the game. I’m an advocate that we should make space for collaboration between everyone. Some may not have the time to travel to a play space for a day, and would not be able to collaborate. My goal was not to change the game or to promote any one kind of collaboration, but to allow for as many types of collaboration possible.

So first of all, let’s address the collaborative guidelines for the first game.

It is done, and submitted. You can play “Survival Mode” through the map, but don’t expect to last more than seconds, and expect other players to kill you before you can get to that screen. It was well worth all the time and hard work spent.

After much work the first map has been added to the “Survival Mode” collection. Map names are:

* Desert Survival
* Ghost Town Survival
* Snow Survival
* Suburban Survival

It is a bit more difficult to be the townie, as you have to hit a few objectives, to go to the “Mobps” screen that allows you to appear “townie,” and then fight the first mob that shows up on the screen. The map allows for plenty of different gameplays, from “sit in the center and let people die,” to get in a high score position, which is the best way to “farm” and have as many teammates as you want. The death screen allows time to organize before you return to the map. With the map having a 10 minute time limit, it lets’s you have a fair start.
